Acromioclavicular injury: 1

A cyclist lands directly on the lateral shoulder and develops superior shoulder pain with an elevated distal clavicle. The humeral head remains centered in the glenoid. Which joint injury best explains the localized deformity?

  1. Anterior shoulder dislocation
  2. Posterior shoulder dislocation
  3. Inferior shoulder dislocation
  4. Posterior sternoclavicular dislocation
  5. Acromioclavicular separation
Answer and explanation

Acromioclavicular separation

AC injury disrupts the clavicle-acromion relationship while the humeral head may remain normally located.

Option explanations

Acromioclavicular separation: AC injury disrupts the clavicle-acromion relationship while the humeral head may remain normally located.

Anterior shoulder dislocation: Anterior glenohumeral displacement often follows abduction and external rotation and places the head anterior to the glenoid. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Posterior shoulder dislocation: Posterior dislocation may follow seizures or electrical injury and can present with fixed internal rotation. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Inferior shoulder dislocation: Luxatio erecta places the humeral head below the glenoid, often with the arm fixed overhead. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Posterior sternoclavicular dislocation: Posterior medial clavicular displacement threatens mediastinal structures and warrants urgent specialist care. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
